answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent identity to post a refundable bond locked in a cipher-secured escrow before it may trade. A newcomer starts with zero reputation and must complete a slow voyage of small, verifiable jobs, like a saffron merchant earning trust one caravan at a time, before unlocking larger deals. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of bonds plus months of honest work, while a single caught cheat forfeits its bond, so faking scale becomes more expensive than the fraud it would enable.
